key_insight: A CMOS+X spiking neuron that pairs a magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) in series with an NMOS transistor can produce biologically realistic, intrinsically nonlinear dynamics, enabling expressive classification without extra circuit overhead.
problem_solved: How to realize compact, energy-efficient nonlinear computation in spiking neurons for classification tasks without adding circuit complexity or large peripheral networks.
method: Design a CMOS+X neuron topology that integrates an MTJ device in series with an NMOS transistor to generate intrinsic nonlinear spiking dynamics.
Use circuit-level simulations to characterize voltage/current trajectories, spike timing, and nonlinear response regimes of the CMOS+X neuron.
Evaluate the neuron's ability to implement nonlinear decision boundaries for classification and compare trade-offs in compactness and energy relative to simpler spiking models.
impact: Provides a hardware-native route to richer neural computations in spiking systems, enabling more expressive, area- and energy-efficient neuromorphic accelerators for ML tasks without adding peripheral circuits.
visual_elements: Circuit diagram showing the CMOS+X neuron: MTJ in series with NMOS, terminals labeled and control signals annotated
Time-series plot of voltage/current and spike events illustrating biologically realistic nonlinear dynamics (e.g., bursting or threshold-dependent response)
2D classification plot showing neural decision boundaries produced by the CMOS+X neuron vs. a linear spiking neuron
Bar or radar chart comparing compactness, energy per spike, and computational expressivity between CMOS+X neuron and baseline spiking neuron implementations
paper_title: Biologically Realistic Dynamics for Nonlinear Classification in CMOS+X Neurons
paper_authors: Steven Louis, Hannah Bradley, Artem Litvinenko, Cody Trevillian, Darrin Hanna
